A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 22-page ARTIST paper, including appendices A–K. Complete text comparison and rendered-page checks support reliable comparison of the text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v2.pdf reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, and supplementary experiments, including accuracy and F1 results in Tables 1–3 and analyses in appendices G–K.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablations, and supplementary experiments reported in v2.pdf, including Tables 1–3 and appendices G–K.

M1.justification: The shared controller-reasoner model, adaptive segment selection, rewards, hierarchical policy optimization, and training procedure are identical in Section 3, Algorithm 1, and the appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the six question-answering benchmarks, extended-length RCW scenarios, and FreqShape and SeqCombSingle evaluations. No dataset, task, or test-scenario coverage changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical throughout the reported experiments, including the main baselines, TimeMaster in Appendix G, PixelReasoner in Appendix H, and TimeX and TimeX++ in Appendix K.

E3.justification: The versions report identical data splits, preprocessing, model configurations, training budgets, metrics, and testing procedures, including the modality, scalability, and explainability evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: Table 3 ablations, Figure 3 utilization analysis, Figure 4 case studies, and the appendix modality, cost, scalability, and explainability analyses are all retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report eight independent evaluation runs and retain the same five-fold mean and standard-deviation reporting in Appendix K and Tables 10–11. No statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 1 reports the same ARTIST average accuracy of 63.61% with SFT and 69.26% with SFT+RL in both versions; appendix results also remain identical.

T1.justification: The mathematical setup, reward definitions, advantage calculations, optimization objectives, and Appendix K metric definitions are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical contributions and claims, including adaptive segment selection, hierarchical collaborative self-play, and the claimed 6.46-percentage-point average accuracy improvement.

C2.justification: Interpretations of selection efficiency, joint optimization, reliability rewards, modality effects, and scalability are unchanged. Both versions retain the same inference-cost and univariate-evaluation limitations.

D1.justification: Implementation details, prompts, data-curation instructions, hyperparameters, hardware, training costs, and listed project and code links are identical. The correspondence-address edit does not revise technical or resource-access instructions.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, and positioning relative to time-series reasoning, dynamic visual search, self-play reinforcement learning, and explainability methods are identical.

P1.justification: On page 1, the correspondence email changes from shvat.messica@fas.harvard.edu to shvat_messica@fas.harvard.edu, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. All other prose and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The updated arXiv stamp is repositioned lower in the first-page margin. Figures, tables, captions, and their placement remain unchanged; rendered pages 2–22 are pixel-identical.

improvement.justification: The revision changes only correspondence information and the first-page arXiv stamp. Scientific content, supporting evidence, reproducibility disclosures, and substantive presentation remain unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
